findings.title: terminal-api refusals made before it identifies the caller carry no acknowledgement, so edge-bff logs them as 'terminal-api older than 3c' and loses the upstream code
findings.root_cause: terminal-api's middleware adds x-terminal-capabilities-applied only when request.state.caller was set (main.py:256-263). The refusals of identify_now come before that: owner header rules in owner_of (400 invalid_owner_headers, main.py:341-371), a key that is neither gateway nor service (401 proxy_key_rejected, :399-405), a key off the private host (403 gateway_host_not_allowed, :319-326). terminal_access.relayed (terminal_access.py:330-333) checks the acknowledgement before the status, so for every principal without '*' these answers are logged only as terminal_capabilities_not_applied with fix 'terminal-api is older than Phase 3c: deploy terminal-api first', never as terminal_refused with status and code. CONTRACT 8b and the terminal-api README say every owner call is acknowledged 'refusals included', which is not true for these answers.
findings.evidence: apps/edge-bff/tests/test_c3c_terminal_checker.py::test_a_refusal_terminal_api_makes_before_it_knows_the_caller_is_logged_with_its_code fails for proxy_key_rejected, gateway_host_not_allowed and invalid_owner_headers; the log is only {'event': 'terminal_capabilities_not_applied', 'status': 401, 'fix': 'terminal-api is older than Phase 3c: deploy terminal-api first'}. Probe against terminal-api's real app (test_phase3c make()): a FREE owner call with a wrong gateway key (401 proxy_key_rejected), an unknown quota name and a lone owner header (400 invalid_owner_headers) all come back without the header.
findings.failure_scenario: With the switch on, TERMINAL_PROXY_KEY is rotated on one side only, or edge-bff sends a header field terminal-api's build refuses. Every free, paid or guest Terminal call answers 503 TERMINAL_UNAVAILABLE (correct for the page), but the log tells the operator to deploy terminal-api first and never names proxy_key_rejected or invalid_owner_headers.
findings.general_class: Mechanism: an acknowledgement that only a data-carrying answer needs is required of refusals too, and is judged before the status, so a diagnostic path hides the real cause. Other sites: the same relayed call serves relay_cut's non-200 branch (main.py:745-751), PageFiles.index and the page grant (pages.py:140, 204). Later tabs: any future relay of a separately deployed service that uses the acknowledgement rule.
findings.fix: In terminal_access.relayed, require the acknowledgement only for a 2xx (a refusal carries no data). Or log the upstream status and code in the not-applied event, and correct CONTRACT 8b and the README sentence 'refusals included' to name the identify-time refusals that cannot be acknowledged.

findings.title: A refused cut download (429 LIMIT_REACHED, 403 CAPABILITY_REQUIRED, 401) reaches the person as 'A data file could not be downloaded (429).'
findings.root_cause: Under 3c a capped plan (the free plan, every guest) is counted when its cut is downloaded. terminal-api's GET /cut and GET /reference/<name>/cut call grant() (main.py:820, :1090), so files_per_hour and megabytes_per_day refuse there. edge-bff relays the refusal correctly (relay_cut -> relayed: 429 LIMIT_REACHED with limit, retry_after_s and Retry-After). The page downloads the cut with rack.ts fetchFile (:90-104), which reads only the status (a leftover of presigned bucket URLs) and throws DownloadError(status). worker.ts:151 forwards its message with no code, and live.ts:186 shows it. Only JSON calls (live.ts api(), fixed for R1-1) map the contract shape.
findings.evidence: apps/edge-bff/terminal/tests/data/c3c_cut_refusal_words.test.ts fails twice: for a 429 LIMIT_REACHED (Retry-After 120) and a 403 CAPABILITY_REQUIRED from the same-origin cut URL, fetchFile rejects with code undefined and the message matching 'could not be downloaded'. The Terminal vitest suite otherwise passes (974).
findings.failure_scenario: A free account or a guest whose hourly file quota is used (for example a private window without the IndexedDB cache) opens the Terminal. /bundle passes (only the ticker quotas are checked there), and the cut GET answers 429 LIMIT_REACHED with Retry-After. The person sees 'A data file could not be downloaded (429).' with no limit and no wait. A plan lowered between /bundle and /cut, or a session that ended, shows the same broken-download sentence instead of the upgrade or sign-in words.
findings.general_class: Mechanism: counting moved from the JSON grant (/bundle) to a byte download, while the byte path still treats every 4xx as a storage-host failure. Other sites: the reference copies (live.ts reference() through the same fetchFile), the Backtest page (re-exports terminal rack.ts), the Watchlist logo list (watchlist/src/api.ts readLogos falls back to monograms silently). Later tabs: any page reading a relayed same-origin file through rack.ts.
findings.fix: In fetchFile, for a same-origin URL with a non-ok JSON answer, read the body with the shared module's readError (as live.ts api() does) and throw a TerminalError carrying the contract code, its words and the wait (401 to the sign-in path). Have worker.ts forward the code. Record it in 3e's scope if it is meant to land there; CONTRACT 8b 'Not in 3c' only says 'the cut beyond what it already reads'.

findings.title: The visitor key reads only the first X-Forwarded-For line, so a client can choose its own key. The record's worst case 'stricter, never wider' is wrong for that case
findings.root_cause: principal.client_of (principal.py:305-320) uses request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for'). Starlette returns the first header line, and client_of takes the right-most entry of that line only. When a request has two X-Forwarded-For lines (the client's own, then one a proxy adds), the client's line decides the address. The address then decides the HMAC visitor key and the per-visitor quotas at terminal-api. throttle.client_address (throttle.py:73-78) reads the header the same way for the sign-in counter per login and address. The assumption 'the right-most entry is the hop the edge added' holds only if the edge appends to the same line.
findings.evidence: apps/edge-bff/tests/test_c3c_guest_recheck.py::test_a_client_written_forwarded_for_line_never_chooses_the_visitor_key fails: 3 visitor keys for one client (TestClient, header list [('x-forwarded-for', forged), ('x-forwarded-for','203.0.113.7')]). The same happens on a real uvicorn server with raw HTTP/1.1 and two X-Forwarded-For lines: the keys differ as the forged first line changes (scratch probe, keys cfb1a391... and 1eda402b...). The records claim the opposite: guest.md 'The client address on Railway' says 'the right-most is the one a client cannot choose ... stricter, never wider'; ERRORS M487 Status says 'worst case without it: every visitor shares one quota, stricter, never wider'. EXEC.md 'Open for the user (asked 2026-11-19): the Railway client-address probe before guests open' presents option (b) on that premise.
findings.failure_scenario: Guests default to on for the live site (config.py Settings.guests, EDGE_GUESTS unset). Suppose Railway's edge forwards a client-written X-Forwarded-For line and adds its own as a second line, or passes the client's header through. Then a script that sends 'X-Forwarded-For: <random>' on each request gets a fresh visitor key each time. It gets fresh terminal-api quotas each time (60 files/hour, 300 MB/day per key) and writes unbounded terminal.access_log rows. The user may choose 'open guests without the probe' because the record says the worst case is stricter. The same first-line reading lets a client choose the address part of the sign-in key (login, address), which is enforced (CONTRACT section 4: 10 failures per login and client address).
findings.general_class: Trust in a forwarded-header layout that has not been proved, read from one header line. Other sites: throttle.client_address (sign-in, registration and email-send counters), and any later per-address limit. A related gap: an IPv6 visitor gets a new key per address, so one /64 gives unlimited keys. Per-address keys for IPv6 are usually taken per /64.
findings.fix: Read every line: ', '.join(request.headers.getlist('x-forwarded-for')), take its right-most entry, and do the same in throttle.client_address. For IPv6, key by the /64 prefix. Make the Phase 0 client-address probe send a client-written X-Forwarded-For header, once as one line and once as two, and record what reaches edge-bff. Correct the worst-case sentence in guest.md, ERRORS M487 and CONTRACT section 2 (line 106), and re-ask the open decision with the correct worst case.
findings.needs_user_decision: The open decision (probe before guests open, or open without it) was asked on the premise 'never wider'. Re-ask it with this case: without the probe, and if the edge keeps a client-written line, quotas per visitor can be widened at will.

findings.title: A visitor's Terminal reads and writes the browser state of an account whose session ended there; the visitor's choices are uploaded into that account at its next sign-in
findings.root_cause: In shared/edge-session.ts session(), when the session read answers 401 and the page allows guests, the module turns the page into a visitor (identity GUEST_IDENTITY). It never compares this with the browser's last-login mark and never clears the previous account's 'user' keys. The design says 'A visitor is never a user of this browser's storage: no last-login mark, nothing cleared' (guest.md section 3). But the Terminal still reads and writes the 'user' keys (ml.ind.favs, ml.ind.v1, ml.assets.v1, ml.symbol ...) through store.set for the visitor. When the account signs in again, noteIdentity sees the same mark, so same=true, and edge-client.js loadPrefs uploads local values that have no server copy. A second effect: with no mark at all, seedKeeps (edge-session.ts) lets user #1 adopt a visitor's state on its first sign-in. Its premise, that markless state can only be user #1's (C3 Phase 1 B1), no longer holds once visitors write these keys.
findings.evidence: apps/edge-bff/tests/test_c3c_guest_recheck_browser.py::test_a_visitors_choice_never_joins_the_account_whose_session_ended_on_this_browser fails. Account ana_free has no preferences. Its session is revoked. A visitor stars indicator I05 in the guest Terminal. Ana signs in again, and edge_bff.user_preferences holds ml.ind.favs ['I05']. In a scratch probe, the visitor's page kept the account's mark (edge-last-login owner:u_...) and its ml.ind.favs, and rewrote the account's ml.assets.v1 from [{t:'BBRI'}] to [].
findings.failure_scenario: On the live site (guests on by default) a shared or family computer: an account's session ends by idle (8 h) or lifetime (24 h) without a sign-out. The next person opens /terminal as a visitor and sees the account's Terminal set-up (favourites, indicators on the chart, remembered choices). Whatever that person changes is written into the account's preferences when the account signs in again. This is the M468/M473/M490 class: browser state not following a change of user.
findings.general_class: A new kind of user (the visitor) added beside the identity marks without being an identity. The rules for a change of user (noteIdentity, checkUser, seedKeeps) assume every writer of 'user' keys is an account. Other sites: every app page that writes 'user' keys and may run for a visitor (only the Terminal today; later guest pages: indicators and more, per decision 1a).
findings.fix: Treat the visitor as an identity. In session(), when the guest read succeeds and lastLogin() names an account, call clearUserState() first, as for another login. Write a visitor mark (for example 'guest:'), so the next account's noteIdentity sees a change and clears the visitor's keys, and seedKeeps never adopts them. Alternatively, keep a visitor's Terminal keys in memory only. Update guest.md section 3 and CONTRACT 4b.

findings.title: An account whose test-account mark is removed keeps using the live site in pre-launch mode: the rule is checked at sign-in only, and --off revokes no session
findings.root_cause: The pre-launch rule (only the admin and accounts marked test_account) sits only in the sign-in route (main.py:860-867). Auth.resolve / accounts.resolve never re-check it. scripts/edge_test_account.py --off (apply(), the off branch) updates users.test_account and writes the audit row, but leaves edge_bff.sessions as they are. CONTRACT section 4 'Sessions' revokes all sessions on disable or role change, but not on this mark.
findings.evidence: apps/edge-bff/tests/test_c3c_guest_recheck.py::test_an_account_whose_test_mark_is_removed_no_longer_uses_the_prelaunch_site fails. After `edge_test_account.py --off` (outcome 'unmarked'), a new sign-in is 403 SIGN_IN_CLOSED, but GET /api/v1/auth/session with the session made while marked still answers 200.
findings.failure_scenario: The main agent removes a test account's mark when the user's test ends (or the user asks to stop an address). The person keeps the live site, with the plan's data, for up to the 24 h session lifetime (8 h idle). The same holds if EDGE_PRELAUNCH is turned back on after a launch: every existing session keeps working.
findings.general_class: A sign-in-time gate with no matching check on the sessions it already allowed. Other sites: any later change of who may sign in (Phase 4 admin disabling of the mark, plan-based sign-in rules).
findings.fix: Either revoke the account's sessions in the --off transaction (UPDATE edge_bff.sessions SET revoked_at = now() WHERE user_id = %s AND revoked_at IS NULL), or apply the rule in Auth.resolve when settings.prelaunch: no session unless test_account, or role_needs_mfa of the resolved capabilities (add users.test_account to accounts.resolve's columns). findings.title: An indicator the plan no longer holds stays drawn: the lock covers the menu's Add only, not the indicators restored from storage, so narrowing the guest plan's rows does not change the chart

findings.title: The two sites' backtest loops share the one-job backtest-worker: one site's hand-over replaces the other site's finished job before its result is fetched (FAILED WORKER_LOST), and a job waiting BUSY uses up its own deadline

POST /v1/jobs answers 409 BUSY while a job runs. A POST that arrives after the job FINISHED replaces it. After that the worker answers 404 UNKNOWN_JOB for every id except the latest, and 410 RESULT_GONE for the replaced job's result (server.ts:16-27, :376-410). The edge-bff follower ends a job FAILED WORKER_LOST on the first 404 or 410 (backtest.py follow :1057-1059, ingest :1132-1134). With two loops, the other site's BUSY retry, made every EDGE_POLL_SECONDS (dispatch :988-995), can land between the finish of this site's job and this follower's next status poll. Its recorded way back is a reset proved by the email code. That reset is refused for 24 h once the address has 20 failed reset codes. CODE_ADDRESS (throttle.py:51, auth_flows.py:206-210) is keyed by the typed address alone and is read before the code, so the right code also gets 429. The reset is unauthenticated, so anyone can type the address. SIGNIN_LOGIN is per (login, client address) at 10 per 15 min (main.py sign_in), so one address reaches the cap in about 2.5 h (75 min over both logins). After each 24 h lock, 10 more tries (15 min) lock again. Both limits on the owner's way in are keyed by public identifiers, and neither has a way out that the stranger cannot close. findings.general_class: Mechanism: a lock and its recovery path both keyed by the same public identifier, each reachable by anyone and neither keyed with the client, so the recovery can be closed by whoever triggers the lock. findings.fix: Key the reset's daily code caps (CODE_ADDRESS, and CODE_USER for resets) by (address, client address), as SIGNIN_LOGIN is. The global bound on guessing a reset code stays with the 5 tries per code and SEND_EMAIL's 10 codes a day (at most 50 guesses a day against 10^6). Alternatively, let a code that matches pass the daily cap. Also consider exempting the right password from the per-account lock when the client's own (login, address) count is clean, or another of NIST's 'additional techniques'. The choice of lock-out policy is the user's (the refuters said so in round 1), so ask with context.
findings.needs_user_decision: Context: on the live site, any account (the test accounts and the admin included) can be kept from signing in by a stranger from one internet address with about 40 requests a day. The account is locked after 100 wrong passwords, and the 'Forgot password?' code that would unlock it is refused after 20 wrong codes typed by anyone for that address. Options: (a) count the wrong reset codes per address and per visitor's internet address, so a stranger's tries do not block the owner's code (recommended); (b) also let the right password through the 100-failure lock when the visitor's own address has no recent failures; (c) keep it as is and accept that strangers can lock accounts out.

verdicts.reason: Not refuted, and I found no serialising layer across sites. claim() picks a QUEUED row with site=%s and blocks it only on another RUNNING job of the same owner_key, in any site. So two owners (the admin on the beta, a test or paid account on live) dispatch concurrently to the one backtest-worker. server.ts answers BUSY only while a job is starting or running. A POST after FINISHED replaces the job: the old id then gets 404 UNKNOWN_JOB, or 410 RESULT_GONE for its result. follow() ends FAILED WORKER_LOST on the first 404, and ingest() does the same on 404 or 410. No lease or advisory lock spans hand-over to result. Not in any record (grep of the fix_round notes and ERRORS for BUSY, replacement and one slot).

verdicts.reason: Mechanism confirmed. A refresh_names failure is swallowed in start_up, and _names_at is set before the query, so for 300 s nothing reads the names again.
